newsitem.title: UK: Crude tanker rates firm, N.Sea star performer.
newsitem.headline: Crude tanker rates firm, N.Sea star performer.

text.p: World dirty tanker rates ended the week steady to firmer overall, shipping brokers said on Friday.

The northeast aframax sector saw the biggest gains over the week with rates for 80,000 tonners on inter-UK/cont trips commanding as much as W155 by the end of the week, against previous rates around W95-100.

"For so long, this market has lagged behind others that a number of owners either fixed or ballasted away, which resulted in a vacuum of available ships," said shipbrokers Galbraith's in their weekly report.
"The short term prospect is for this market to remain high as there are simply fewer vessels available," the report said.
Shipping brokers said Mobil had fixed an 80,000 tonner for a Sture/Britain trip at W155, loading May 29, while Elf fixed a similar vessel and trip at W137.5 loading May 28.
Elsewhere, tanker rates were steady to slightly stronger.
Very, large crude carriers (VLCCs) doing Middle East/Japan trips commanded between W60-65.
"With many charterers still awaiting confirmation of their June stem dates the market is expected to rise next week.

"In fact our estimate of only 40 vessels of about 12.5 million tonnes being potentially available will also underline an anticipated rise in the market," shipping brokers Gibson said in their weekly report.
The Mediterranean experienced a subdued fixing week with 80,000 tonners on cross-Med trips fetching between W100 to W105 while 130,000 tonner ranged from W85 to W95.
The West African market was also thin but rates were steady.
"Although million-barrel enquiry form West Africa was thin between low to mid-W90s was maintained for all destinations, said shipbrokers at Gibson in their report.

They said that VLCCs had fared better with five fixtures concluded, two for the U.S. Gulf in the mid-W60s and three to the Far East at rates in the low to mid-W50s. -- Melanie Goodfellow, London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7714.
